subject: Civil Engineering
title: Rainfall and Runoff
description: A quick win: understand Rainfall and Runoff.

hook.text: An inch of rain on a square mile produces 17 million gallons of water. Where does it go?

buildup.text: Some rain infiltrates the ground. Some evaporates. The rest runs off into streams.

discovery.text: The runoff coefficient measures what fraction becomes runoff — pavement is near 1.0.

twist.text: Urbanization increases runoff dramatically — concrete and asphalt don't absorb rain.

climax.text: Hydrographs plot runoff over time — a bell curve that peaks hours after the storm.

punchline.text: Pave the ground and rain becomes a flood instead of groundwater.

quiz.question: Why does urbanization increase stormwater runoff?
options: Cities generate more rainfall due to heat island effects
Impervious surfaces like concrete and asphalt prevent rain from infiltrating the ground
Urban areas are always built in low-lying flood-prone locations

details.summary: Rainfall-runoff analysis converts measured precipitation into the surface water flow that infrastructure must convey. Engineers use design storm events, intensity-duration-frequency relationships, and hydrological models to predict peak flows and total runoff volumes for sizing drainage systems.
details.whyItMatters: Accurate rainfall-runoff prediction determines whether drainage systems can handle storms or streets will flood. Underestimating runoff causes flooding; overestimating wastes construction budgets.
takeaways: The rational method estimates peak runoff for small catchments using area, intensity, and coefficient
Intensity-duration-frequency curves relate rainfall intensity to storm duration and return period
Urbanization increases runoff by replacing permeable surfaces with impervious pavement

faq.question: What does a 100-year storm actually mean in engineering terms?
faq.answer: A 100-year storm has a one percent probability of occurring in any given year. It does not mean it happens only once per century. Two 100-year storms can occur in consecutive years.

faq.question: How does urbanization change rainfall-runoff relationships?
faq.answer: Impervious surfaces like roads, roofs, and parking lots prevent infiltration, converting nearly all rainfall to surface runoff. Peak flows increase dramatically, runoff arrives faster, and total volume increases.
